text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), after withdrawing its first group of observers due to monitor Albanian polls on Sunday, then decided to also scrap a second delegation from its parliamentary assembly, after the Albanian government rejected part of its team list.

- OSCE secretary general Robert Olivier said the withdrawal of its second 19-strong group of monitors for Albania's Sunday local polls would weaken the credibility of the whole election monitoring process.
- Germany has also withdrawn its small team of three observers in protest at Albania's decision not to allow the OSCE team to monitor the elections.
- A court has ordered the arrest of four more people charged with collaborating with a crime ring, including the son of a former Democratic Party justice minister.

- The paper, quoting an article from London-based The Economist magazine, says it would be a catastrophe if pyramid schemes in Albania collapsed since seven in 10 Albanian families have trusted their money to such schemes.
- An ethnic Albanian Yugoslav citizen was sentenced to ten months in jail for selling works of late hardline communist dictator Enver Hoxha.
- A 20-year-old man wounded seven schoolchildren when his tractor smashed through the school's courtyard in the eastern region of Korca before he was overpowered by villagers.

- The opposition Socialist Party candidate for mayor of Tirana, Agim Fagu, says his aim is to renew the confidence of Albanians in government ethics, as he plans to govern independently of the Socialists' influence.
- About 500 foreign observers will be watching Sunday's municipal elections in Albania.
